bibliographic.title: A Categorical Archive of ChatGPT Failures
bibliographic.citation_apa: Borji, A. (2023). A categorical archive of ChatGPT failures. Research Square. https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-2895792/v1

methodology.method_family: descriptive failure taxonomy based on ChatGPT interaction examples
methodology.study_design: categorical archive of observed ChatGPT failures
methodology.sample_description: ChatGPT responses and interaction examples organized into failure categories
methodology.technology_context: ChatGPT; large language models; chatbots; dialogue systems; conversational agents; question answering

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article directly analyzes ChatGPT as a conversational dialogue system and catalogs eleven failure categories including reasoning, factual errors, math, coding, and bias, while highlighting risks, limitations, and societal implications. This supports risk-oriented governance discussion, but the provided text does not evidence operational governance mechanisms, regulated-domain deployment, audit/compliance controls, or human oversight frameworks.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial sections were supplied; full methodology, complete failure taxonomy, sampling procedure, and governance-relevant implications require verification in the full PDF.

appraisal.notes: Objective is clearly stated, but the excerpt does not describe systematic sampling, inclusion criteria for prompts, or analytic procedures beyond categorical presentation. Limitations about model versioning are acknowledged.

cerqual.explanation: The study offers a coherent failure-oriented account of ChatGPT relevant to conversational AI risk, but available text provides limited detail on data collection rigor, sample scope, and governance mechanisms, reducing confidence for central evidentiary use.

coding.theme: Taxonomy of failures in ChatGPT conversational interactions
coding.subtheme: Risk and limitation catalog for dialogue-system LLMs

synthesis.main_claim: ChatGPT exhibits recurring failures across eleven categories, and a structured archive of these failures is needed to understand risks, limitations, and societal implications of conversational LLMs.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a categorical archive of ChatGPT failure types to help researchers and developers improve future language models and chatbots.
synthesis.limitations: Failures may no longer exist in newer ChatGPT versions as the technology improves; the archive is positioned for comparison and synthetic data generation rather than as a governance framework.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on conversational LLM failure modes and risk/limitation themes; not sufficient as central evidence on conversational governance, compliance, or operational controls in regulated settings.
